answer: The prism test I would run is Gem cutter drilled bead assay witnessed by the jewel charter: each drilled bead is a mine assay countersigned by the warden, so a farm must cut a hundred real gems by hand, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. Running a hundred clones would mean a hundred separate proofs, each costing real money and real time, and the ember of that bill is larger than anything one epoch pays out. The quartz is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
